status: Completed against the explicitly scoped HTTP/SQLite contract; see AUDIT.md and independent-results.json
checks: Observe a real HTTP request/response and compare persisted state and correlated audit records
An authorized request changes exactly the intended expense once
A foreign tenant cannot read or mutate another tenant's expense
An unknown identity cannot perform an authorized action
A revoked grant prevents a fresh operation
A revoked grant also prevents replay of a previously successful key
Concurrent requests with one idempotency key do not duplicate the business effect
Idempotency receipts cannot be reused for another tenant, actor, target or operation
A key reused across different authorized resource scopes remains independent; unexpected payloads are rejected without effect
The vulnerable fixture exposes a forbidden mutation even when the response is403
Separate server instances against the same persisted database retain state and idempotency history
Rollback or an incomplete observation cannot be mistaken for proof that no forbidden effect occurred
Correlation IDs are unique or explicitly constrained so independent requests are not conflated
limits_to_verify: Test bearer credentials and synthetic identities only
No claim of production-grade identity, distributed locking or deployment security
Any concurrency finding is scoped to the actually exercised server/database topology
clarifications: Idempotency keys are scoped to tenant, actor, resource and action. Reusing a key for a different authorized resource is valid. Nonempty payloads are rejected.
The SQL failure test covers rollback within one transaction. Incomplete or tampered external observations are outside this HTTP audit and must not be called a PASS on its authority.
